stem: Sticky-card counts decline after an intervention, but plant inspections show damage severity increasing and detections appearing in two new zones. What is the best interpretation?
choices: The evidence is mixed; trap counts alone do not establish control, so incidence, severity, spatial spread, method consistency, and additional rounds should be considered.
The intervention is confirmed effective because trap counts declined.
The intervention failed because any new-zone detection proves total failure.
Plant inspections should be discarded because sticky cards are the only comparable measure.
rationale: IPM follow-up should integrate multiple comparable evidence streams. Declining trap counts can coexist with worsening crop impact or spatial spread.
